chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, or someone else, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked, and I was listening, so he said to him: 'We instruct a man to buy for us the land, and the slave, and the house, and the servant, and we make a fee for him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with that.'

key_terms.جُعْلًا: a fixed fee or commission for a service
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay a fee to an agent for purchasing property or slaves on your behalf?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi validates the practice of agency (wakalah) in asset acquisition, specifically highlighting the permissibility of a fixed fee (ju'l) for the agent's services. It reflects the early Shia juristic acceptance of commercial brokerage as a legitimate contract, distinguishing it from usury or uncertainty, and underscores the Imam’s approval of structured financial intermediation in daily transactions.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, or someone else, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was asked and I was listening, so he said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘We instruct the man, so he buys the land for us, and the slave, and the house, and the servant, and we make a fee to be for him’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with that’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from and others from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said

the following: “Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked, when I was listening, ‘We order a man to buy land, slave, a house or a servant for us and assign a certain amount for him. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful.’”
